about: An alternative picture pipeline: shoots a film-crew board inside Unreal Engine 5 as real 3D space instead of compositing it in PIL. The board's flat artwork becomes textured planes stacked in depth, lit unlit, and photographed by an orthographic CineCamera driven from Sequencer — so parallax, depth of field and camera travel are produced by an actual camera moving through a set rather than by scaling layers on a canvas. Runs fully headless via UnrealEditor-Cmd; no editor UI, no C++ module, Blueprint-only project.

provides_renderer.name: Unreal Engine 5
provides_renderer.about: Flat 2D artwork staged as planes in a real 3D scene and captured with AutomatedLevelSequenceCapture. Substitutes for the style's own renderer at compile, render and shoot; changes nothing else about the production. Buys true parallax and camera optics at the cost of a heavier, slower render.

briefing.compile: Compile the beat plan into the style's storyboard as usual — the storyboard is renderer-neutral — then run scripts/board_to_ue.py to translate it into a UE level plus Level Sequence. Judge the result with the look test (one held frame per shot, tiled) rather than a PIL contact sheet. Pass --motion-plan through to the style's compile exactly as normal; the Unreal stage reads the compiled board, not the plan.
briefing.render: Render with UnrealEditor-Cmd -game -MovieSceneCaptureType=...AutomatedLevelSequenceCapture writing PNG frames, then encode with ffmpeg. Detect and trim the black warm-up frames instead of hard-coding a skip count — the count varies with scene content. Verify format, loudness and motion exactly as usual.
briefing.shoot: Re-photograph the same set for the vertical Short by swapping the camera's aspect and re-framing, not by re-authoring the staging. The set is 3D, so a 9:16 crop is a camera decision.
